instructions: Peel the potatoes, halve them lengthwise and slice them 1/4 inch thick. Roughly chop the onion.
Heat 1/3 cup of the oil in a 10 inch nonstick pan over medium heat for about 2 minutes. Add the onion and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until it's soft.
Add the potatoes and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Cook for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring every 2 to 3 minutes, until they're golden and a slice breaks easily when you press it.
Meanwhile, whisk the eggs in a large bowl with 1/2 tsp of the salt and the pepper.
Make the aioli too. In a small bowl, stir the 1/2 cup mayonnaise with the garlic grated in, 1 tsp lemon juice and the last 1 tbsp oil. Chop 2 tbsp of the chives.
Transfer the potatoes and onion into the eggs with a slotted spoon, leaving the oil in the pan. Stir and let it sit for 2 minutes.
Put the pan back over low to medium heat. Pour in the egg mixture in an even layer and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, without stirring, until the underside is golden and the edges are set.

Slide the tortilla onto a flat plate about the size of the pan, then flip it back into the pan. Press the edges in toward the middle and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until just set. That should be about right when the center no longer jiggles.
Slide it onto a board and cut it into 8 wedges.
Cut the baguette into four 6 inch pieces and split each one lengthwise. Spread the aioli on both cut sides, add 2 wedges to each and scatter on the chives.
Serve warm or at room temperature. To pack it, keep the wedges and the aioli apart in the fridge for up to 3 days and fill the bread just before eating.
method_notes: Spain on a Fork cooks the potato and onion slowly in olive oil, folds them into whisked egg, cooks the tortilla in a nonstick pan, flips it and serves wedges in a split baguette with garlic mayonnaise and chives. That Spicy Chick (5 from 4 ratings) fries the potatoes faster with a strain over a bowl and mentions butter or mayonnaise in the bread. Nothing read had 20 ratings, so it follows the Spain on a Fork bocadillo page, which has no rating. At about 50 minutes this is not a 30 minute lunch; the tortilla keeps, so it suits being made the night before.
